rob2_provisional: D1 — Randomization process
SOME CONCERNS — PROVISIONAL
Prospective registry, statistician-generated permuted blocks and concealed sequence are strengths.
Cluster-to-individual randomization changed after first enrollment; implementation for all randomized participants is not established from public abstract.
Full article/CONSORT flow and dated allocation implementation.
D2 — Deviations from intended interventions
SOME CONCERNS
Primary analysis planned as ITT; outcome collectors were blinded.
Participants, nurses and clinicians were unblinded; real-world CGM and nurse exposure may differ.
Full fidelity, contamination and cointervention results by arm.
D3 — Missing outcome data
SOME CONCERNS — DENOMINATOR HOLD
Protocol prespecified responder/nonresponder checks and possible MI/IPW above 10% attrition.
92% and n=230/259 are arithmetically inconsistent; arm-specific missingness and implemented methods are unclear.
CONSORT denominator, arm-level missingness and executed sensitivity analyses.
D4 — Measurement of outcome
SOME CONCERNS
Masked outcome collection and a prespecified self-report instrument.
Primary outcome relied on 12-month recall in unblinded participants; intervention could affect awareness or reporting.
Exact administration, missing-item handling and equal measurement by arm.
D5 — Selection of reported result
SOME CONCERNS
Trial registered before enrollment and primary binary outcome remained identifiable.
Secondary/analysis details changed during follow-up; clustering clarified after completion; public protocol lacks an explicit multiplicity statement.
Version-dated SAP implementation and full result-table reconciliation.
Overall
SOME CONCERNS — PROVISIONAL, MAY ESCALATE
No evidence of fabricated randomization or switched primary outcome was identified.
Multiple unresolved domains jointly affect confidence; final judgment cannot be sealed.
Close D1, D3 and D5 gates with full article/analysis documentation.
